title: Find Orphan Sales
description:
Some overnight `product_id`s are not in the merchandising catalog yet. Ops wants **only those orphan sales** — not the matched ones.

**Left-anti-join** sales (`INPUT_PATH`) against products (`PRODUCTS_PATH`) on `product_id`. Keep sales rows with no catalog match. Do not emit product columns. Write Parquet with overwrite.

Sales columns: `txn_id`, `product_id`, `store_id`, `quantity`. Products columns: `product_id` (unique), `product_name` (unused in output). Output: the four sales columns only. Use an explicit left anti join (`how="left_anti"` or `"anti"`) — a left join would keep matches with null names; an inner join would keep only matches. Implement with Spark DataFrame APIs — no driver-side nested loops over `collect`. **Run** uses two smoke testcases; **Submit** uses the full set and row-diffs your Parquet against each case’s `expected/`.

Write results with `df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(OUTPUT_PATH)`. `OUTPUT_PATH` is set by the platform for **this Run/Submit only**.

problemStatement.overview: Left-anti-join sales to products on product_id; keep only unmatched sales; write Parquet to OUTPUT_PATH.
symptoms: Ops cannot isolate new SKUs that never hit the catalog.
A left join keeps matched rows too; an inner join keeps only matches — neither is the orphan list.
yourTaskSteps: Read sales from INPUT_PATH and products from PRODUCTS_PATH.
Left-anti-join on product_id so only unmatched sales remain.
Write txn_id, product_id, store_id, quantity (no product columns) to OUTPUT_PATH with overwrite.
Submit is graded with a row-level compare against each selected testcase expected/.
problemStatement.yourTask: Implement src/main.py that finds orphan sales via left_anti.
hints: left_anti keeps left rows with no match and does not add right-side columns.
left_semi is the opposite filter (exists); left keeps all sales with nullable names.

gradeChecks: Spark job succeeds on selected Submit testcases
OUTPUT_PATH Parquet readable with sales columns only (no product_name)
Each Submit testcase expected/ matches candidate rows (key + values)
No extra rows beyond the union of selected expected testcases
